title: quercus faginea var. submembranacea
intro: Quercus faginea var. submembranacea, commonly known as the Portuguese oak, is a variety of the Quercus faginea species, a type of evergreen tree native to the Iberian Peninsula. The Portuguese oak is valued for its rich source of bioactive compounds, which have been used in traditional medicine to treat various health conditions. The health benefits of Quercus faginea var. submembranacea include its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to protect against cardiovascular disease, reduce oxidative stress, and combat infections. The bioactive constituents of the Portuguese oak include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which have therapeutic actions such as scavenging free radicals, inhibiting lipid peroxidation, and modulating the immune system.
